name: Vantage Data Centers cooling posture: liquid-to-the-RACK today, liquid-to-the-chip only as a build-to-suit engagement
price_basis: No published pricing. Build-to-suit liquid-to-chip deployments are quote-only engagements with their own construction timeline, and that construction timeline is the real cost - see notes.
notes: THE MOST IMPORTANT COLO RECORD IN THIS SLICE, BECAUSE IT DISTINGUISHES TWO COOLING TECHNOLOGIES THAT ARE ROUTINELY CONFLATED AND THAT DECIDE DEPLOYABILITY. Vantage's own words: 'Vantage has utilized various cooling technologies since our inception, including air-cooled chillers, water-cooled chillers, indirect heat exchange and liquid to the rack. We are committed to an air-cooled chiller model as our preferred design moving forward.' And on going further: 'Vantage is also partnering with customers to bring liquid to the rack in large scale applications. We're making advances toward pushing the medium for heat exchange closer and closer to the source-i.e., the chip-with a goal of an even more efficient, and just as reliable, cooling approach based on our customers' unique needs. This application is ideal for a build-to-suit data center.' READ THAT CAREFULLY. Their 50 kW+ tier is LIQUID TO THE RACK - a coolant loop delivered to the rack enclosure, typically serving in-rack heat exchangers or rear-door heat exchangers. It is NOT liquid-to-the-chip, i.e. not a direct-on-die cold plate fed by a CDU. NVIDIA's GB200 NVL72 needs the latter: the DGX GB guide specifies liquid running up and down the rack through manifolds and then through cold plates attached to the CPUs and GPUs inside each sealed 1RU compute tray. Different plumbing, different failure domains (their guide devotes a section to leak detection), different water temperatures, different maintenance contracts. A facility that can do liquid-to-rack may still not be able to accept an NVIDIA rack-scale system without construction. Their Highlights point the same way: 'Pre-tapped headers to provide liquid to the FLOOR' and 'Forging a liquid-to-the-chip future' - present-tense aspiration, not a shipped standard. THE COMMERCIAL CONSEQUENCE: liquid-to-chip at this density is a BUILD-TO-SUIT project, not a product you order. The lead time to deploy a GB200 NVL72 into an existing colo building is therefore dominated by construction, not by GPU supply, which inverts the usual assumption that lead time is set by the accelerator. Facilities engineering, not procurement, becomes the critical path.
